messages.subject: model simplification in path analysis
parts:
Dear All,

I'm doing a path analysis using lavaan and I would have a few questions related to model simplification. 

I built a saturated model tracing all paths between my variables, based on data from literature and also my own experience. Based on the P values obtained from the saturated model (P>0.1), I use a step-wise elimination of non-significant paths, obtaining in this manner the final path model. 
I compared models with different path structures using the AIC value (the smallest value indicating the best model fit). 

My questions would be the following:

1. Related to the syntax used in lavaan. Which one of these is the correct syntax to do the model simplification, 'path.model.version1' or 'path.model.version2'? Eliminating paths should be done simply by deleting them, or excluding them from the model using "0*" syntax? 

path.model.version1 <- 'ww ~ ug+ 0*smi + 0*fdb + 0*sex
                      smi ~ sex                  
                      ug ~ 0*smi + 0*sex 
                      fdb ~ ug + 0*smi + 0*sex'

path.model.version2 <- 'ww ~ ug
                      smi ~ sex                  
                      fdb ~ ug'

2. During the model simplification process, do I have to compare somehow the differently structured models? (e.g. Chi-sqr test, or Anova, etc.) 

Thank you in advance!

Best wishes,
Attila

parts:
On 04/25/2014 02:07 PM, Fülöp Attila wrote:

> My questions would be the following:
>
> 1. Related to the syntax used in lavaan. Which one of these is the
> correct syntax to do the model simplification, 'path.model.version1' or
> 'path.model.version2'? Eliminating paths should be done simply by
> deleting them, or excluding them from the model using "0*" syntax?
>
> path.model.version1 <- 'ww ~ ug+ 0*smi + 0*fdb + 0*sex
> smi ~ sex
> ug ~ 0*smi + 0*sex
> fdb ~ ug + 0*smi + 0*sex'
>
> path.model.version2 <- 'ww ~ ug
> smi ~ sex
> fdb ~ ug'

The second one only uses a subset of the variables. You can not compare
version 1 vs version 2. From what you describe, you need version 1: all
the variables, but some paths fixed to zero.

> 2. During the model simplification process, do I have to compare somehow
> the differently structured models? (e.g. Chi-sqr test, or Anova, etc.)

It seems you are using path analysis in an exploratory fashion. Usually,
we use a confirmatory approach, and we only test those models that we
have pre-specified.

Note that all model respecifications may work for your particular sample
only. That is, the changes may not generalize to new samples.

Yves.
